items.title: Neural network study sheds light on how AI chatbots 'reason' like humans
items.excerpt: Yale computational linguist Tom McCoy and Microsoft/NYU co-authors (arXiv) show LLMs' internal vectors can be swapped for role-and-filler symbolic representations with little behavior change, and targeted edits to them steer outputs, which suggests that symbolic-like structure emerges on its own.

items.title: Spiking neural network learns to predict what will happen, when, and how likely it is
items.excerpt: University of Tokyo WPI-IRCN researchers (Communications Biology) built a 1,000-neuron recurrent spiking network that uses only local learning rules to learn which event a cue predicts, when it arrives and how likely it is, adapting when probabilities shift, with implications for neuromorphic AI.

items.title: AI helps identify drilling regimes with a projected potential increase in drilling speed of up to 68%
items.excerpt: Skoltech's Shadfar Davoodi (Results in Engineering) pairs LSTM/random-forest surrogates, SHAP explainability and NSGA-III optimization on 5,738 well records to find carbonate-reservoir drilling settings, projecting up to a 68.4% faster penetration rate. These are surrogate estimates that still need field validation.

items.title: Pollen study reveals the hidden history of grasses
items.excerpt: University of Illinois researchers (PNAS, 'Deep learning of fossil pollen morphology') combine super-resolution microscopy with convolutional neural networks to tell grass pollen apart, estimating species diversity and C3/C4 grasses across a 25,000-year Mount Kenya lake-sediment record.

items.title: Nobel physics winner's pride at pioneering AI role
items.excerpt: New physics Nobel laureate Francis Halzen, creator of the IceCube neutrino observatory, recalls proposing AI for data analysis in 1991 and says neural networks and machine learning are what finally revealed the Milky Way in IceCube's neutrino data.

items.title: AI chatbots endorse existing climate-related policies twice as often as new proposals
items.excerpt: A University of Waterloo study (Environmental Research Communications) ran ~55,000 prompts through 11 LLMs and found they endorse existing climate policies ~70% of the time versus ~34% for new proposals, and recommend EVs less often than they actually sell in the regions studied.

items.title: Using AI for just 10 minutes erodes your ability to persist at hard things
items.excerpt: Across three randomized trials with 1,222 participants (UC Berkeley, presented at COLM), people who used an AI helper for ~10 minutes became less persistent and less accurate on fraction and SAT reading problems once it was removed, often giving up, while never-assisted participants did better by the end.

items.title: Now in Nature: Retrofitting language models to operate over bytes
items.excerpt: The 'byteification' technique behind Ai2's open byte-level Bolmo models, published in Nature with LMU Munich, Cambridge, UW and Imperial, converts existing tokenized LLMs to letter-by-letter models with under 1% of usual training, preserving performance and fixing character-level tasks like spelling backward.

items.title: Is AI the End of Math As We Know It?
items.excerpt: Mathematicians are meeting AI's sudden advance on proofs with grief, anger and a search for new ideas. One warns: 'If we don't adapt, there's just no more math in 50 years.'

items.title: How AI helped bring an ancient tomb dating to before the Roman Empire back to life
items.excerpt: Researchers paired artificial intelligence with acoustic technology to reconstruct an Etruscan tomb, the Tomb of the Blue Demons, giving a new view of a burial site that predates the Roman Empire.

items.title: How attachment theory can help us understand AI relationships
items.excerpt: Psychologists apply attachment theory, the framework for life's most significant relationships, to explain why people form emotional bonds with AI companions and what those bonds mean.

items.title: Drones, AI and the future of wildlife conservation
items.excerpt: Robotics and machine learning are opening new possibilities for protecting wildlife around the world, Physics World reports.

items.title: This light-powered AI can spot deepfakes with nearly 98% accuracy
items.excerpt: UCLA researchers built an optical AI system that uses light to analyze more than a dozen videos simultaneously, detecting deepfakes with nearly 98% accuracy, with high speed, low energy demand and resistance to attacks.

items.title: The effects of an “algorithmic monoculture” depend on the details
items.excerpt: MIT research finds that many firms using a single hiring algorithm ('algorithmic monoculture') is less harmful to job seekers than earlier work suggested, and can even help, depending on the details.

items.title: Who we become when we talk to machines
items.excerpt: In her new book 'Artificial Intimacy,' MIT sociologist and psychologist Sherry Turkle argues that chatbot companionship harms people psychologically at every stage of life.

items.title: We’re putting too much faith in AI’s ability to say no
items.excerpt: Today's LLMs are engineered to refuse dangerous requests, but refusal is far from foolproof and could become an instrument of repression, the op-ed argues.

items.title: OpenAI mistranslated mathematics into code for its Navier-Stokes proof
items.excerpt: OpenAI's surprise Navier-Stokes solution came as one proof for humans and one formal version for computers, and New Scientist reports that the two do not match: the mathematics was mistranslated into code.

items.title: Scientists can't stop using AI, even when forbidden from doing so
items.excerpt: When scientists were asked to review papers for a conference without using AI tools, many of them ignored the request and used AI anyway.

items.title: OpenAI claims we've entered the AGI era — has GPT-6 Astra really demonstrated general intelligence?
items.excerpt: OpenAI says GPT-6 Astra brings humanity to the threshold of AGI, but external evaluators argue that inflated lab metrics and opaque testing obscure its true reliability.
